endangerment.comment: Michif (1755-crg) = Severely Endangered (80 percent certain, based on the evidence available) (No parents speak the language to their young children, but some grandparents use it with their grandchildren.) [Bakker 2013](cldf:bakker:13)

classification.sub: Michif is classified as a Plains Cree variety with a very large number of French loans. French-derived words in Michif have Cree stress patterns (and possibly also vowel length and nasality) **hh:phon:Zykoski:Michif** and several elements of the noun phrase are Cree-derived (animacy-alienability-demonstratives-quantifier syntax-derived nouns-adnominal relative clauses) as is the loss of elision and behaviour of articles **hh:s:Rhodes:French-Cree**, **hh:svsoc:Bakker:Michif**. Verb stems of French origin occur but usually need a derivational verbalising affix **hh:s:Rhodes:French-Cree**, **hh:svsoc:Bakker:Michif** in a manner similar to many other languages borrowing verbs. See also **hh:typ:Gillon:Michif:2018**:7-8 **hh:s:Rosen:Michif**:983.
